summary: Built the CS2-style HUD for SimBuild as pure DOM inside #ui (src/modules/ui/{index,hud,icons,styles,showcase}.js + bundled CC0 Aileron font in src/modules/ui/fonts/). Bottom dock: toolbar with 14 inline-SVG coloured category icons (roads, zoning, landscaping, props, bulldoze | 8 service categories shown locked | info views), milestone chip with XP bar, RCI demand bars (R/C/I/O, driven by world.economy.demand and sim:demand), right-side overlay/statistics/photo buttons; status strip with play/pause + 1x/2x/4x speed (calls clock.pause/resume/setSpeed), HH:MM clock and month/year date, weather chip (sun/moon/cloud/rain + temp + season), city name, population/happiness/money chips with trend arrows. Category sub-panels (CS2-style asset cards with costs, tool-mode/elevation/snapping option box, tool hint pill), info panel on selection:changed (building/road/node/prop/vehicle from world data, level stars, detail rows, status bars, Focus/Policies/Demolish), top-right notification stack (typed, auto-dismiss via dt, HTML-escaped), tiny mono dev corner (wall-clock fps, frame ms, draws, tris, textures) with showcase and camera switchers. Every interaction emits ui:action; tool:changed highlights the category/card; modules.tools?.api?.select?.() / setOption?.() called safely; Esc/Space keyboard shortcuts. Showcase: all panels open with sample data (road panel, selected 'Linden Terrace' building, three notifications) over a 4-draw backdrop (PBR grass ground with distance fade, merged asphalt/sidewalk street grid with lane markings and kerbs, instanced procedural facades with per-window night lights, instanced trees, park block in the street/closeup camera corridor) and a 'ui' camera preset. Final gauntlet (shots/ui/rdev2/summary.json): 16 shots, 0 console errors, maxDrawCalls 11, maxTriangles 219,044, minFps 0 (SwiftShader frame starvation; one closeup shot hit the tool's 30 s screenshot timeout and passed on an immediate re-shoot). Core/tools nits filed in docs/core-requests/ui.md. In-game the UI itself costs 0 draw calls; the declared budget (16) covers the showcase backdrop.
